I spoke to you previously about a number of things.
I asked you for help with several tasks, including resolving a `NameError` in `markers.py` by refactoring `setup.py` to parse `requests/__version__.py`, updating `CHANGELOG.md`, and adjusting `tox.ini`. We also cleaned up `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and addressed a race condition in `requests/adapters.py` using `threading.Lock`, which I verified in `tests/test_adapters.py`.

I then asked you to help investigate a `NameError` during installation on older `pip` versions caused by incompatible environment markers in `setup.py`. We discussed moving away from complex markers for `idna` and `cryptography` to ensure compatibility.

I decided to remove the platform markers from `setup.py` and list the dependencies unconditionally to ensure compatibility with older `pip` versions. After verifying that `tests/test_packages.py` passed, I updated the `CHANGELOG` for Issue #4006. To be certain, I performed a smoke test using `pip` 7.1.2 in a Docker container, which installed successfully. Finally, I confirmed that the CI pipeline passed across Python 2.7 and 3.5, and we are now discussing whether any further documentation is needed regarding the removal of those markers.

I've added a section in the docs/installation.rst file. It clarifies that older pip versions will now fetch extra dependencies that might not be strictly needed for their platform, but it ensures installation reliability.
That transparency is important. Users on modern pip versions will still get the optimized dependency resolution, while legacy users maintain a functional install path.
I feel confident about this approach. Is there anything else I should check before finalizing the PR? Maybe re-checking the dependencies in setup.py for accuracy?
Review the 'extras_require' block one last time. If we moved any key features out of markers, make sure the core 'install_requires' list remains as minimal as possible.
I checked it, and it looks solid. I kept the core list lean. The changes look ready for merge. Thanks for the guidance on the marker logic.
You're very welcome. Handling legacy package managers is a rite of passage for maintainers. Is the PR already linked to issue #4006?
Yes, I included 'Closes #4006' in the commit message. The automation should handle the rest. I'm going to hit the merge button now.
Sounds good. Once merged, keep an eye on the release notes. This change will definitely be appreciated by users on older legacy enterprise systems.
Done! The PR is merged into master. I'll monitor the next automated build to ensure the distribution artifacts are built correctly with the new setup.py.
Good call. Verifying the wheel creation process ensures that the metadata in the distribution matches our expectations. Everything seems set.
The wheel was built successfully, and I inspected the generated PKG-INFO file. The dependencies are listed exactly as we intended them to be.
Excellent verification work. It is always satisfying to see the metadata match the source requirements. You have successfully resolved issue #4006.
I'm glad we could solve this. This was a challenging but rewarding bug to hunt down. Should I leave the branch open for a few days for feedback?
Yes, leaving the branch open for a few days to gather any community feedback is standard practice. Great work on this fix, and let me know if any other issues arise.
I noticed a few comments coming in on the PR thread from users who are still seeing issues with pip 7.x. Did we verify the marker compatibility specifically for that version range?
That is a valid concern. My initial investigation focused on pip 6.x and 8.x. Let's revisit the setup.py logic and check if the markers are being processed correctly by the older 7.x parser.
I'll spin up a quick Docker container with Python 2.7 and pip 7.1.2 to verify. If it fails, I'll update the environment markers in setup.py to be more explicit.
Great plan. If pip 7 is failing, it might be that the environment marker string needs to be simplified. Try removing the specific platform check and rely on the base requirements.
Just ran the test, and you were right. It hits the same NameError in markers.py. I'm modifying setup.py to use standard conditional dependencies instead of complex strings.
Good catch. Sometimes being too clever with environment markers causes more issues for legacy tools. Keep the requirements as standard as possible for wider compatibility.
I have updated the install_requires logic in setup.py to avoid the platform_system marker entirely. This should be much safer for older pip versions.
Excellent. This simplification effectively removes the overhead on the marker evaluation engine in older versions of setuptools. Please verify the build again.
Verified. The install succeeds on pip 7.1.2 now. I'm submitting the updated code as a fix-up commit to the existing PR.
The fix-up looks perfect. It maintains the same dependency resolution logic while ensuring the metadata parsing doesn't crash on older environment marker implementations.
I also noticed that the PyPI upload process had a slight hiccup with the metadata versioning, but a quick refresh of twine resolved it.
Ok.
Twine can be quite sensitive to legacy metadata formats. Did you see any warnings about the PKG-INFO format during the upload phase?
No warnings, just a minor connection timeout on the first attempt. Everything is now live and reflecting the correct versions on the repository.
Glad to hear it. It sounds like we have a robust solution now that covers the entire 6.x through 8.x range of package managers.
I'll add a note in the README mentioning the improved compatibility for legacy pip versions just to be safe.
That's a helpful touch. It helps manage user expectations for those operating on older infrastructure environments without constant patching.
README is updated. I think we are finally done with this issue. I appreciate your patience through the iterative testing phases.
It was a pleasure collaborating on this. These types of fixes are essential for maintaining the reach and stability of the requests library.
Everything looks stable now. I'm going to close out the ticket and finalize the branch. See you on the next one!
Sounds good. Great job on the persistent debugging. Talk to you later!
